frozen_claim: In sparse non-Hermitian synaptic matrices, transient dynamics and effective memory capacity are governed primarily by the non-normality of the operator (pseudospectrum / Kreiss constant / numerical radius), not by the eigenvalue distribution: two ensembles with an identical eigenvalue spectrum but different sparsity-induced non-normality will show systematically different transient amplification and memory.

observable.name: transient_and_memory_governance_at_fixed_spectrum
observable.definition: Three pre-registered measurements on synthetic operators A = Q (D + s*T) Q^T with real orthogonal Q, a block-diagonal real Schur D that fixes the eigenvalues, and a strictly BLOCK-upper-triangular T that raises non-normality while leaving the spectrum exactly fixed. (A) At a fixed eigenvalue spectrum (spectral radius held at 0.85), sweep the Henrici departure 0->27 and measure the worst-case transient amplification sup_t||A^t||_2 over t=1..400. (B) Pool 16 operators varying BOTH spectrum and non-normality and regress log sup_t||A^t|| on each candidate predictor (log Kreiss constant, log numerical radius, log departure, spectral radius); compare R^2. (C) At an IDENTICAL spectrum (radius 0.9) compare memory capacity of a normal operator (departure 0) versus a non-normal delay-line chain (departure ~5.9) in a noisy linear reservoir with Ridge readout. The claim is supported for transients iff the spectrum-pinned amplification rises with non-normality and a pseudospectral measure (Kreiss) dominates the spectral radius as predictor; the memory half is supported only if the non-normal operator stores systematically MORE at identical spectrum.
observable.source_ref: arXiv:2606.00326 (Ansari & Shukla) — seed paper characterising the eigenvalue spectrum of sparse synaptic matrices; the duel tests a mechanistic alternative (non-normality, not the spectrum, governs transients and memory) on synthetic controlled-spectrum operators, not on the paper's observable as measured on biological connectomes.

model.generative: A = Q (D + s*T) Q^T. D is a block-diagonal real Schur matrix whose 2x2 blocks fix a target eigenvalue spectrum; T is strictly BLOCK-upper-triangular (zeros within the diagonal Schur blocks) so that scaling s raises the off-block coupling (non-normality / Henrici departure) while leaving every eigenvalue, and thus the spectral radius, exactly unchanged. The naive strictly-upper perturbation that touches the 2x2 diagonal blocks is rejected because it moves the spectrum it is meant to fix.
model.config: Experiment A: N=100, spectral radius target 0.85, departures 0..27 (7 levels). Experiment B: N=80, 16 operators over 4 spectra (rho 0.6,0.75,0.85,0.92) x 4 non-normality levels. Experiment C: N=100, spectral radius target 0.9, normal vs delay-line chain. Diagnostics: Henrici departure; sup_t||A^t||_2 (t=1..400 in A, 300 in B); numerical radius (180 angles); discrete-time Kreiss constant on a finite grid (24 radii x 72 angles) outside the unit circle; memory capacity via a noisy linear reservoir (single fixed input vector, Ridge readout, noise 1e-2). numpy 2.4.4, deterministic seed 17.
model.controls: Spectral-radius invariance is the central control: max absolute deviation of the spectral radius across all non-normality levels is 0.0 (the block-upper perturbation preserves the diagonal Schur blocks exactly), so any change in transient amplification cannot be attributed to a moving spectrum. The normal operator (departure 0) is the matched control in Experiment C at the identical spectrum.

thresholds.ci: exact within float64; single deterministic seed=17 (no stochastic sampling in the decisive constructions)
thresholds.decision_rule: The transient half is supported iff, at a spectral radius pinned exactly at 0.85, sup_t||A^t|| rises monotonically with non-normality AND, over the 16-operator pool, R^2 of log sup on log Kreiss >= 0.9 while R^2 on spectral radius <= 0.2. The memory half is supported only if the non-normal chain stores systematically MORE memory than the normal operator at the identical spectrum (radius 0.9); it is NOT supported if the chain stores the same or less.

nulls: spectral_radius held exactly fixed (max abs deviation 0.0) so transient growth cannot be an artifact of a drifting spectrum.
normal operator at the identical spectrum (departure 0) as the matched control for the memory comparison.
failure_modes: Synthetic controlled-spectrum operators cannot establish that real sparse synaptic matrices live in this regime (external validity) — the decisive limitation of this test.

The Kreiss constant is approximated on a finite grid outside the unit circle (24 radii x 72 angles); the reported value is a lower bound on the true supremum, sufficient for rank-ordering and regression but not exact.
sup_t||A^t|| is computed over a finite horizon (t=1..400 in A, 300 in B); for spectral radius < 1 the peak is captured before decay.

Memory capacity is measured in a simplified noisy linear reservoir (single fixed input vector, Ridge readout, noise 1e-2); input direction, readout structure and nonlinearity can change the picture — the memory result is contested and is NOT a clean confirmation of the thesis.
Experiment C uses one specific delay-line chain construction; it shows memory differs at an identical spectrum but does not establish that non-normality monotonically governs memory.
accepted_evidence_criteria: The transient half of the thesis is supported if, at a spectrum pinned exactly at radius 0.85, the worst-case transient amplification rises with non-normality and the Kreiss constant explains the (log) transient variance far better than the spectral radius (R^2 Kreiss >= 0.9, R^2 spectral radius <= 0.2), with spectral-radius invariance confirmed (max abs deviation 0.0).
rejected_evidence_criteria: The thesis as a UNIFIED real-data claim is NOT established by this synthetic test. The memory half is rejected as overreach if the non-normal chain stores the same or LESS memory than the normal operator at the identical spectrum. The whole thesis would be falsified on real data if, on biologically sampled sparse synaptic ensembles with the spectrum strictly controlled, pseudospectral measures failed to dominate transient amplification or memory.

sensitivity_grid.kreiss_grid: 24 radii x 72 angles outside unit circle
